title: Structured log queue with trace-anchor and backfill coordinator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Our current log ingestion path has three gaps that surface during heavy traffic and schema migrations: 1) out-of-order trace linkage when logs from secondary collectors arrive late, breaking span->log correlation for critical traces; 2) schema evolution causing silent drops or partial parsing for new structured fields; 3) inability to safely backfill historical events into Loki/ELK without replay storms or double-ingest. This ticket implements a convergent queueing layer and a backfill coordinator that attach stable trace anchors and enforce schema versioning at ingress.
technical_summary: Introduce a broker-agnostic inbound queue (Kafka consumer group + optional SQS adapter) that enriches each message with a trace_anchor header derived from available trace/span IDs and a compact schema_version tag. The queue persists a minimal idempotency key and ingestion watermark for each tenant-shard and feeds a set of deterministic workers (ingest workers) that validate schema compatibility, apply lightweight transformations, and write to downstream sinks (Loki append API + ES bulk). The backfill coordinator runs as a separate controller that throttles replays by tenant, honors existing watermarks, and emits safe cutover markers so the Console and dashboards can avoid double-counting during migrations.
approach_options: Option A: Broker-stateful queue with per-tenant watermarks stored in Redis. Pros: low latency, easy lookups; Cons: added operational surface and potential single-point of failure.

Option B: Persistent watermark and idempotency in a small write-optimized Postgres table with optimistic concurrency. Pros: strong consistency and easy migrations; Cons: higher write amplification and cost under heavy ingest.

Option C: Fully stream-native design using Kafka compacted topics for watermark and idempotency. Pros: scales with traffic and is operationally aligned with existing Kafka usage; Cons: requires careful partitioning and increases coupling to Kafka semantics.
Decision: Prototype Option C for scale and alignment with existing infra, keep Redis fallback for low-latency metadata caching (hybrid).
acceptance_criteria: New ingestion queue accepts structured logs with schema_version header and emits validation metrics (valid/parsing_errors) to telemetry.
Trace-anchor header is present on all downstream writes; Console trace lookup can link logs to spans for >99% of sampled traces in canary tenants.
Backfill coordinator supports tenant-by-tenant replay with configurable rate limits and does not cause duplicate writes when run with idempotency keys.
End-to-end canary against three test tenants (low/medium/high throughput) shows <5% added 95th percentile latency on ingestion path and no increase in downstream error rates.
Runbook and rollback steps documented; feature guarded behind a runtime flag per cluster/tenant.

Service: ingest worker that validates schema and emits to Loki/ES adapters

rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal QA runs with synthetic traffic (1 day). Stage 2: Canary deploy to two non-production clusters with three tenants each (toggleable per-tenant flag). Stage 3: Gradual enablement for production tenants grouped by traffic class (low -> medium -> high) over 2 weeks with monitoring gates. Global kill-switch to revert to legacy path if parsing_errors > 1% for 10m window.
test_plan: Unit tests for trace_anchor derivation and idempotency; integration tests that simulate out-of-order arrival and verify trace linking; property tests for schema version negotiation; load test to validate watermark store under 10k messages/s; backfill dry-run to assert no duplicates using idempotency keys.

notes: Keep the schema_version numeric and increment-only. Avoid auto-migration at ingest time — transformations should be opt-in per tenant. Backfill coordinator must emit a reconciliation report per run and persist a replay checkpoint to avoid partial replays.
